newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-KIWIS SNATCH LAST-GASP VICTORY OVER BRITAIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-KIWIS SNATCH LAST-GASP VICTORY OVER BRITAIN.

text.p: Former All Black
winger John Timu scored two tries in the final 10 minutes as New
Zealand came from behind to beat Great Britain 17-12 in the
first test in Auckland on Friday.
The Kiwis trailed the tourists 12-4 when British replacement
Adrian Morley was sent to the sin bin for an illegal tackle.
From the next play, Timu split the defence and dived over
for his third test try, converted by Matthew Ridge.
New Zealand took the lead when Timu ran on to a wide pass
and scored in the left-hand corner. Ridge converted, and added a
field goal for good measure in the dying moments of the match.
First-half tries from Alan Hunte and Denis Betts helped
Britain to a 10-2 halftime lead, which they extended after the
interval with a Bobbie Goulding penalty.
Ridge pulled it back to 12-4 with a penalty and only
desperate British defence foiled efforts from both Ridge and
Timu.
Morley's dismissal proved the turning point with a weary
British side unable to plug the gap.
The two sides meet again in Palmerston North next week in
the second game of the three-test series.
Teams:
New Zealand - Matthew Ridge (captain), Sean Hoppe, Richard
Blackmore, John Timu, Richard Barnett, Gene Ngamu, Stacey Jones,
Grant Young, Syd Eru, Quentin Pongia, Steve Kearney, Tony Iro,
Tyran Smith.
Britain - Stuart Spruce, Alan Hunte, Kris Radlinski, Daryl
Powell, Anthony Sullivan, Iestyn Harris, Bobbie Goulding, Paul
Broadbent, Keiron Cunningham, Terry O'Connor (replaced by Chris
Joynt), Denis Betts, Paul Sculthorpe (Adrian Morley), Andy
Farrell (captain).
